message: Hey Karla. Understood on moving forward quickly with an initial prototype. I'm definitely comfortable handling both the mechanical and electrical side of things. For mounting. I don't foresee needing to use any metal mounting hardware for the motors themselves. The torque should be easily handled. I would be comfortable working on a 3-4 week time line.

To address your concerns ab out stability. it will have a solid base with rubber/TPU feet to prevent any rattling or moving about. The initial build will be as simple as possible using off the shelf components for the electronic side of things. The mixing performance will be reliable as we will use a motor that can handle the load of the liquids easily. I could have a BOM available within 24-48 hours.

Hey Larry — this sounds great, I like the approach and timeline.

Let’s move forward.

For the first step, I’d like to focus on:
• system layout
• motor + component selection
• basic wiring plan

Goal is to get a working prototype up and running as quickly as possible, then refine from there.

Let me know what you need from me to get started.

Do you plan on plugging this into a standard 120v wall outlet or do you prefer it be powered off 12v like a car battery? If any other questions do happen to arise I'll promptly let you know. I'm ready to begin the CAD work and begin putting a bill of materials together. Everything is ready on my end to proceed. Thank you and I look forward to working with you on this project.

Tricky? How so?

Well if I'm not mistaken you want the motor to be under the bowl with the mixing head protruding through the bottom, as of now I plan on putting a hole directly into the center of bowl for that mechanism. The drainage hole will need to be offset from that some and it may leave some liquid in the bottom after fully draining.
Is there any way to work around this and still have a smooth and efficient process?
If we update the design to look like this, A) would the pouring be more efficient? B) Would it be a simpler build? C) Would it change the timeframe?

Yes that would make pouring more efficient. It would be a simpler build as we don't have to deal with potential leakage in a shaft seal with the other method. Going to a build like this should not affect time frame negatively.

Ok. Let's go with this design. It still keeps alive the DJ Turntables vibe. Let's make the pour spot should be facing the baristas. I want the buttons to be functional and work. Let's try and make it as splash free as possible. Keep the words on the machine the same. Green accents. The only difference is I want it to say "Karla's Matcha Mixer". From the side view I like the thickness of the machine. I want deep matcha wells but I don't want the box to be too big.

For the spout design, I want to make sure:
• There’s a clean open/close mechanism (no dripping)
• It’s properly sealed to prevent leaks into the base
• It’s easy to clean between uses
• The pour flow is smooth and controlled

Curious what your approach would be for implementing that in a simple, reliable way for V1.

Key Design Details
1\. Valve / flow control

I don’t want:

constant dripping
uncontrolled pouring

I need 👉

a simple open/close valve or tap

2\. Seal at the bottom

This is critical.

👉 The bowl must:

not leak
not seep into electronics
3\. Cleaning

Matcha + milk = residue

👉 The spout should be:

removable OR
easy to flush/clean
4\. Flow rate

Don’t want:

slow drip
or explosive pour

👉 Smooth, controlled stream

Let me look over everything here and I'll come up with a fresh approach on this and get back with you shortly. • better mixing quality

• faster visual cycles during events

One small tweak to consider

That way I can pre-prep and swap bowls fast during events
Also, I want to go with the color beige for the design. The bowl size here is fine.

Powered by the 120v to 12v 20A Dc power supply and independent PWM speed controllers. Each station features 12v 200rpm motors connected to 3/8" shaft couplings to a 3/8" stainless steel shaft. Hey Larry — I went through the BOM and overall I really like the direction. This is exactly what I was hoping for.

A few thoughts I’d like your input on before we move forward:

• Motors — I’m wondering if 200 RPM might be a bit low for achieving a strong, frothy matcha texture. Do you think it makes sense to increase RPM while still maintaining enough torque for smooth mixing?

• Whisk — would a stainless steel or milk-frother-style head perform better than the resin whisk in terms of consistency, durability, and foam quality?

• Spout — I’d like to stick with the solenoid approach. It’s important that the pour is clean, controlled, and seamless (mix → open → pour) both for texture and the overall visual experience.

• Splash / mess control — this is really important for events. I want to make sure:
– minimal to no splashing during mixing
– smooth, controlled flow from the spout (no sputtering)
– no dripping when the valve is closed
– good sealing so nothing leaks into the base
– some form of splash guard or lip around the bowl if needed

• Cleaning — I’d like the bowls and spout components to be easy to clean or removable if possible.

Everything else looks great to me. Curious to hear your thoughts on these and if you’d adjust anything before we finalize the BOM.

For the motors, I believe you are right about the speed. I've selected some new ones that will spin at 1000RPM. The PWM controller will still allow the speed to be adjusted from 0 up to 1000 while still maintaining the torque to mix the liquids. 

The whisk portion is tricky, there aren't a lot of options with the requirements we need. You want a decently sized mixing head to ensure the bowl is mixed well. The bowl is approximately 9 inch in diameter while the plastic mixing head on the BOM is only around 2.4" diameter. The original wire whisk I suggested was around 4.5" in diameter. Despite it being listed for a 6qt bowl, I do think it has the potential to work well in our smaller bowl. I think the ideal mixing head would be similar to the handheld electric frothers/mixers but those heads only come in very small sizes. 

I don't foresee splashing to be an issue. The motors can be adjusted on the fly if the mixing becomes too rough. If splashing is an issue a simple splash guard can be installed as you suggested.

For cleaning, as of now the bowl is designed to be removed very simply. I also plan to allow for the custom spout to be removable for easy cleaning as well. 

Overall I think we are nearly ready, I'll change the motor to 1000rpm. For the whisk, perhaps we should pick 2 styles to test which works best? The whisk is probably one of the easiest components to swap to new design if needed. A simple adapter should let us attach basically any whisk to our setup.

I've found another whisk which may work. Its the same diameter as the resin whisk from amazon but made of stainless steel. I could cut the handle off of it and adapt it to the shaft. <https://www.amazon.com/Digead-Stainless-Versatile-Blending-Whisking/dp/B088TH4QDV>

The shaft can be shortened to length on them. <https://www.amazon.com/Motor-3000RPM-Output-Replacement-Electric/dp/B0GCZS9PVK>

I think 3000 RPM works as long as we’re not running it at max all the time. Having the flexibility to dial it in for different mixing levels (slow mix vs higher-speed frothing) is actually ideal.

One thing I do want to make sure of with the higher RPM:
• we keep splashing under control
• the mixing stays smooth and doesn’t get too aggressive at higher speeds

So if needed, I’m open to adding a splash guard or dialing in whisk position / bowl depth to make sure it performs cleanly.

Overall I’m good with this direction.

Great.

A couple things I want to make sure we dial in as you refine the layout:

• Bowl removal — I want to make sure the bowls can be lifted out easily without interference from the whisk or motor assembly.

• Whisk removal — ideally something quick and simple to detach (no tools if possible), since cleaning and swapping during events will be important.

• Whisk positioning — I think getting the height right will be key for both foam quality and minimizing splashing, especially with the higher RPM range.

• Splash control — since we’re going with a stronger motor, I want to make sure the system stays clean during operation (either through positioning, bowl geometry, or a subtle guard if needed).

Everything is looking great — just want to make sure we get these usability details right for real event use.

I'm currently considering a simple "twist lock" design for the whisk itself. Making the whisk simple to remove is going to be key for the bowl removal as the whisker is going to be directly in the way of removing the bowl. Typical mixers solve that by having a mixing head that tilts upwards. I'll test multiple whisk heights and depths to see what gives the most consistent and best result for the mixing itself.

Hey Larry — I went through the finalized BOM and everything is looking really solid. I like the direction a lot and I think we’re very close to locking this in.

I just had a few quick things I wanted to confirm before I move forward with ordering parts:

• Motors — I noticed the listing mentions an eccentric output shaft. Just want to confirm that this will still give us a smooth, centered rotation for the whisk, or if we should consider a straight/centered shaft for better stability.

• Motor performance — I like the move to 3000 RPM for flexibility. I just want to make sure we’ll be able to dial it in for smooth mixing and avoid overly aggressive splashing at higher speeds.

• Solenoid flow — since we’re using on/off valves, do you expect the pour to be smooth when opening, or will it release too abruptly? I want to make sure we get a clean, controlled pour without splashing.

• Power supply — with both motors, solenoids, and fans running, are we comfortably within the limits of the 12V 20A power supply under load?

• Splash control — with the higher RPM, I just want to confirm that whisk positioning, bowl depth, and overall layout will keep things clean during operation. I want this to be as splash-proof and mess-free as possible for events.

Everything else looks great to me — just want to make sure we’re fully dialed in on these before the order is placed.

Let me know your thoughts.
Also, the spouts. You said you would fabricate those yourself? I don't see them on the BOM.

For the motors, the eccentric output shaft is actually a typo from the previously selected motor. The new one has a centered shaft. 

The solenoid flow should be smooth. The 1/2 outlet should prevent any liquids from releasing abruptly. 

It would probably be wise to step up to a higher output power supply. That way there is reduced risk of anything overheating and overloading. In addition to the power supply, higher rated PWM controllers would also be beneficial for the same reason of overheating.

In regards to the spouts, those are going to be fabricated out of 1/32 stainless steel. You will find that material at the very bottom of the BOM.
